title: Region Isolation Controls, Retention Guardrails & Failover Proof Automation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement deterministic controls and automation for private/VPC/on-prem data residency and retention plus a tamper-evident evidence/reporting pipeline that runs during normal operations and when a regional failover or evacuation is initiated. Goals: 1) ensure per-customer region constraints and retention windows are enforced by control-plane routing and node-level policy; 2) produce an auditable, signed evidence bundle (logs, config snapshots, proof-of-residency assertions) whenever data moves or failover occurs; 3) add configurable quarantine/warmup constraints to prevent accidental cross-region residency during emergency failovers.
acceptance_criteria: Control-plane API enforces region constraints: requests for customers with region-locked policy are routed only to allowed pools; any attempt to route outside allowed regions fails with explicit error and is auditable.

Retention guardrails implemented: per-customer retention TTLs are respected by both hot cache eviction and cold-store lifecycle jobs; retention override requires documented operator approval recorded in audit log.

Failover automation respects quarantine window: automatic failover to alternate region only after configurable quarantine/warmup checks or explicit operator approval; default quarantine configured to 15 minutes for region-locked customers.

Evidence/reporting pipeline generates a signed bundle within 60 minutes of a failover event or policy change, containing immutable manifests, S3 object hashes, gateway audit logs, and topology snapshots.
Console and API expose residency decision and evidence link for each failover event; customers with private deployments can download the signed bundle.
E2E tests that simulate regional evacuation, retention edge cases, and operator-approved override pass in CI; security review and pen test completion recorded before release.
Automated alerts created: if evidence bundle generation fails, on-call is paged and the system falls back to a queued retry with SLA of 1 hour.
Dependencies to existing residency orchestration components are verified; integration tests with routing and KV cache validated.
Documentation (Confluence + runbook) and release notes prepared and linked from the ticket.
Benchmarks: evidence bundle generation does not add >2% latency overhead to normal request path and storage cost estimates accounted for in cost model.
tasks: Design: finalize data model for region policies, retention TTL, and operator approval metadata (Confluence: /confluence/display/RES/Region+Policy+Model).
Runtime: implement routing guard in smart-router to check customer.policy.allowed_regions before assigning a request to a worker pool.
Node-level: extend node agent to enforce retention TTLs for cached KV and to refuse writes if node is out-of-compliance with residency policy.
Failover flow: implement quarantine timer and warmup checks (topology health, capacity checks, KMS access validation) before promoting alternate region.
Evidence pipeline: create evidence-generator lambda/pipeline to collect logs, snapshots, S3 manifests, sign bundle with HSM-backed key, and store index in evidence-store.
Console/API: surface residency state, failover events, and signed evidence bundle links; add 'download proof' button for private deployments.
Automation: on failover trigger, kick evidence pipeline and attach bundle ID to incident timeline; create retry/alert logic.
Tests: unit, integration, and chaos test scenarios to simulate forced evacuation, manual override, and TTL expiry during migration.
Privacy/Legal: coordinate with compliance and legal to validate proof format and retention of evidence bundles.
Documentation: runbook for on-call to follow when evidence pipeline fails and for operator approval workflow.
Release: feature flags gating rollout to private customers; phased enablement with telemetry to monitor policy rejections and false positives.

notes: This ticket focuses on the enforcement and proof aspects of residency and retention. Separate work exists for regional capacity orchestration (separate project). Ensure minimal user-facing API changes for hosted customers; primary impact is private/VPC/on-prem tenants.
implementation_risks: Race conditions between cache eviction and failover snapshotting could produce inconsistent evidence if not coordinated.
Signing keys must be protected and access audited; HSM integration will add ops complexity.
False positives in policy enforcement could disrupt customer traffic — require careful rollout with canary group and fast rollback path.
Storage costs for evidence bundles need to be capped and lifecycle-managed (retention of proofs should be configurable).
